lecture_summary: The lecture develops circular multi-body gravitational orbits. It derives the period of a binary-star system about its common center of mass, uses symmetry and force components to find the speed of three equal masses orbiting in an equilateral configuration, and calculates the system’s total energy to determine whether it is gravitationally bound. The central strategy is to distinguish pair separation from orbital radius, then set the net inward gravitational force equal to mv²/R.

videos.title: Gravity, Universal Gravitation Constant - Gravitational Force Between Earth, Moon & Sun, Physics
videos.reason: Reviews Newton’s inverse-square law and includes a multi-body net-force example, providing the best foundation for both the binary and three-mass calculations.

videos.title: Center of Mass Physics Problems - Basic Introduction
videos.reason: Supports locating the binary’s common center of mass, finding its unequal orbital radii, and recognizing the equilateral system’s center by symmetry.

videos.title: Addition of Vectors By Means of Components - Physics
videos.reason: Covers the component method needed to show that tangential gravitational-force components cancel while inward radial components add.

videos.title: Speed of a Satellite in Circular Orbit, Orbital Velocity, Period, Centripetal Force, Physics Problem
videos.reason: Best match for the lecture’s central dynamical move: gravity supplies mv²/R, while v = 2πR/T connects orbital speed and period. It supports both the binary-period and three-body-speed derivations.

videos.title: Mechanical Energy - Basic Overview
videos.reason: Provides the distinct E = K + U framework used in the lecture’s final bound-system calculation without repeating the selected orbital-dynamics material.

coverage_gaps: No playlist entry directly treats two comparable masses orbiting a common center of mass, derives T² = 4π²d³/[G(M+m)], or emphasizes that the mutual separation differs from either body’s orbital radius.
No entry directly covers three equal masses rotating at the vertices of an equilateral triangle, including the symmetry result Fnet = √3Gm²/L², R = L/√3, and v = √(Gm/L).

The energy selection is only a general match: no listed video explicitly covers U = −Gm₁m₂/r with zero at infinity, counting each unique gravitational pair once, or interpreting negative total energy as gravitational binding.
